Figure 37 delves deeper into the relationships between built parameter, build direction, and post-fabrication heat treatment by manufacturer, offering a nuanced understanding of the dataset. A closer examination of Figure 37a reveals the frequency distribution of specimens across different built parameters for the two manufacturers, PAC and Praxair. A notable trend emerges, with PAC demonstrating a higher overall frequency of specimens across all build parameters compared to Praxair. Furthermore, each build parameter exhibits a relatively consistent frequency within each manufacturer, with parameter 1 being the most prevalent choice for both PAC and Praxair. This insight suggests that manufacturer-specific preferences may be at play, influencing the selection of built parameters and ultimately, the properties of the resulting specimens. Figure 37 (b) illustrates the distribution of build direction (horizontal “H” and vertical “V”) for the specimens manufactured by PAC and Praxair. For both the manufacturers, a significantly higher number of specimens are built vertically (V) compared to horizontally (H). Figure 37 (c) displays the distribution of specimens that underwent either “As Built” (AB) or "Heat Treatment" (HT) after fabrication, categorized by manufacturer. PAC has a much higher frequency of specimens in the “AB condition compared to those that underwent HT; whereas all the specimens fabricated by Praxair are AB. The probability distribution of specimen thickness, as shown in Figure 38 (a), indicates a left skew, with most data points concentrated around a thickness of 0.00100 m. There is a prominent peak at this thickness, signifying that it is the most frequent value in the dataset. The distribution is relatively narrow, suggesting that most specimens fall within a close range of thicknesses, with a few outliers on the thinner side. In contrast, the distribution of specimen width, depicted in Figure 38 (b), is highly right- skewed, with the vast majority of specimens having a width close to zero.
